intro: THE LAST SIGNAL. Chapter 1: The Signal.

Six hours ago, dispatch picked up a signal on an emergency band. Three short tones, one long, over and over. They traced it to a research facility on the north road. A place that has been dark for a long time.
You used to work there. You left two years ago, became a police officer, and did not look back. Tonight, the call came to you.
THE LAST SIGNAL. Chapter 1: The Signal.

Six hours ago, dispatch picked up a signal on an emergency band. Three short tones, one long, over and over. They traced it to a research facility on the north road. A place that has been dark for a long time.
You used to work there. You left two years ago, became a police officer, and did not look back. Tonight, the call came to you.

summary.text: You learned his name: Daniel.
Daniel opened the way down for you.
You found your own way down.

effects.say: You hold the door open and step back out. The facility is still waiting. Take the elevator again when you are ready.

intro: THE LAST SIGNAL. Chapter 2: Preservation.
The elevator falls for longer than one floor should take. When it stops, the silence is different down here: thicker, colder, closer.

summary.text: Emily Carter is alive, asleep in the medical ward.
Emily Carter is alive, still in her capsule in the preservation lab.
Emily Carter died.
You told Daniel that Emily is alive.
You sent Daniel the preservation records.
You agreed to wake Prototype 001.
You refused to wake Prototype 001. For now.

effects.say: You stand in the quiet a while longer. There is still time to look around, and Emily still needs looking after.

intro: THE LAST SIGNAL. Chapter 3: Awakening.
You come back to the storage room. The shape under the grey tarp has not moved. The speakers crackle before you can decide anything.

summary.text: You woke Prototype 001. It called you an intruder.
You reminded 001 what it was built for. It hesitated.
You took the key from 001 while it slept.
You are still hurt from 001’s grip.
Daniel admitted he had believed Emily left him.

effects.say: You step back out of the lift cage. Somewhere on this floor, heavy footsteps keep their slow rounds.

intro: THE LAST SIGNAL. Chapter 4: Remains.
The lift settles at the bottom of its shaft with a long metal groan. Somewhere far above, 001’s footsteps keep their slow rounds.

summary.text: You let Daniel watch over Emily.
You wired Emily’s ward into Sublevel 2’s power.
You told Daniel his body is still breathing.
You woke Emily.
Emily and Daniel spoke for the first time in two years.
You are carrying 001’s original core, the one Daniel wrote.

effects.say: The machines hum on. There is still time to look around.

intro: THE LAST SIGNAL. Chapter 5: Relocated.
You ride back up from Sublevel 2. Somewhere above you, Daniel is listening. Somewhere, the rest of him is waiting.

summary.text: Emily told you something she never told Daniel. You kept it.
You are carrying Emily’s lanyard for Daniel.
You told Daniel you were coming, against his wishes.
Someone from the board has visited the isolation door recently.
You found Daniel.

effects.say: You stand in the doorway. Behind you, the stairwell. In front of you, Daniel. Nothing has to happen yet.

intro: THE LAST SIGNAL. Chapter 6: The Board.
You step into the isolation room. The door stays open behind you. You make sure of that.

summary.text: You gave Daniel Emily’s lanyard.
You kept Emily’s secret for her to tell.
You told Daniel something Emily never said.
You gave 001 back the core Daniel wrote. It remembered Emily.
You learned that 001 carries a copy of Daniel’s mind.
You arrested Marcus Hale.
Marcus Hale agreed to help undo what he signed, and then answer for it.
You let Daniel have his revenge on Marcus.

effects.say: You take a breath. The rain keeps falling.

intro: THE LAST SIGNAL. Chapter 7: The Last Signal.
You come back down the stairwell. The door is open. He is waiting.
THE LAST SIGNAL. Part Two. Chapter 1: Summons.

summary.text: Emily and Daniel finally said it.
You asked for a lawyer.
You told Detective Ruiz everything about the facility.
You lied to Detective Ruiz, and she caught it.
Emily and Daniel are your alibi.
Your alibi is a man in a machine.
You have no alibi.
The tip with your name came in hours before the body was found.
Daniel says it wasn’t him.

effects.say: The cell is quiet. Morning is a long way off.

intro: THE LAST SIGNAL. Part Two. Chapter 2: Witnesses.

summary.text: You told Sarah you are noticing now.
You and Sarah are friends. For now.
Emily vouched for Sarah, and laughed at you.
Emily will testify.
Daniel will testify.
Marcus will testify against his own board.
Theo, the night guard, will testify.
Ana will testify.
Priya is terrified, and coming anyway.
Priya walked away.
Pryce was about to testify against the board.
The signal came from inside the courthouse.

effects.say: Okafor is still on the phone. The rain has not stopped.

intro: THE LAST SIGNAL. Part Two. Chapter 3: The Trial.
Three days later. Courtroom 4. Every seat in the gallery is taken.

summary.text: Theo recognised the prosecution’s witness, Victor Lane, as the board’s private security.
Ruiz admitted your radio vanished from the evidence room.
Marcus told the court that Pryce was about to testify against the board.
You took the stand.
Okafor thinks the jury is with you.
Okafor says it could go either way.
Okafor will not meet your eyes.
Someone kept a copy of everything. Including him.

effects.say: The courtroom is empty except for the people waiting with you.

intro: THE LAST SIGNAL. Part Two. Chapter 4: The Verdict.

summary.text: The jury found you not guilty.
The jury found you guilty. Then Ruiz walked in with your radio, and it was over.
The voice is Dr. Helena Voss, chair of the board, living in the facility network.
Voss holds the master copy of Daniel’s mind, and wants a body.
You told her you are coming to fight.
You told her you would think about her deal.

effects.say: The courthouse is closing. Sarah is waiting by the door.

intro: THE LAST SIGNAL. Part Two. Chapter 5: Static.

summary.text: You made sure the voice on your radio was really Sarah.
You told Sarah her voice was keeping you sane. She told you how you walk.
You did not fall for Voss using Sarah’s voice.
Voss’s voices cost you time.
You saved the last copy of Daniel.

patrol_car.name: Patrol car, outside the facility
patrol_car.description: You sit in the driver’s seat of your patrol car with the engine ticking as it cools. Rain drums on the roof. Through the windshield, the research facility is a dark block against a darker sky. Two years ago you walked out of that building and promised yourself you would not come back.
patrol_car.revisit: Your patrol car. Rain on the roof, the radio murmuring, the facility waiting outside.

listen.text: Rain on the roof, heavy and even. The engine ticks. Under the hiss of your police radio, faint and patient, the signal repeats: three short tones, then one long one.

actions.label: Listen to the radio
actions.text: Dispatch is quiet tonight. Between transmissions you can hear it again: three short tones, one long. It has been repeating on an emergency band for six hours, and it is coming from the building in front of you.

actions.label: Review the call notes
actions.text: You flip open the notepad clipped to the dash.
actions.afterText: The call notes are in your journal.

actions.label: Open the glovebox
actions.text: The latch sticks, then gives. Inside: registration papers, a dead lighter, and your flashlight. You test it. The beam is strong.
actions.afterText: Registration papers and a dead lighter. Nothing else you need.

exits.label: Step out into the rain
exits.text: You pull up your collar and step out. The rain finds you immediately.

front_gate.name: Front gate
front_gate.description: A chain-link gate stands half open, its padlock hanging from a cut chain. Beside it, a small guard booth with a tin roof. Beyond, a short path leads to the glass doors of the main building. No lights anywhere.
front_gate.revisit: The front gate. Rain on the guard booth’s roof. The building ahead, the car behind.

listen.text: Rain on the guard booth’s tin roof, sharp and close on your left. Ahead, from inside the building, a thin pulse of static: the same pattern dispatch heard.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: The chain was cut cleanly, with bolt cutters. The cut ends are rusted. Whoever did this did it a long time ago.

actions.label: Search the booth
actions.text: The booth smells of wet paper. A clipboard hangs on a nail by the window: the visitor log.
actions.afterText: An empty chair, a dead phone, and the nail where the visitor log hung.

reception.name: Reception lobby

description.text: The lobby is cold and smells of dust and old rain. Grey light from the doors behind you shows the shape of a long front desk ahead, a directory board on the wall to your left, and a staff photo board beside it. A doorway on your right is marked SECURITY. Straight ahead, past the desk, the main corridor disappears into total darkness.

Emergency lights paint the lobby a dull red. The long front desk sits ahead, the directory board and staff photo board on your left, the security office door on your right. The main corridor ahead is lit now, faintly.

reception.revisit: The reception lobby. Front desk ahead, security on your right, the corridor straight on.

details.text: Somewhere on the front desk, a small light is blinking. Three short, one long.

text.text: Water drips somewhere to your left. Ahead, on the front desk, a little speaker crackles in rhythm: three short tones, one long. The signal is coming from right here.
Water drips somewhere to your left. The building creaks as the wind leans on it. Nothing else answers.
Papers swollen with damp, a dead monitor, and a charging dock with one handheld facility radio still in it. Its status light blinks three short, one long. The radio’s speaker hisses in time with it.
Papers swollen with damp, a dead monitor, and an empty charging dock.

actions.label: Take the facility radio
actions.text: You lift the radio out of the dock. The blinking stops. The hiss stops. For a moment the lobby is completely silent.

actions.label: Read the directory
actions.text: Plastic letters on felt, a few fallen to the floor.
actions.afterText: The directory is copied into your journal.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: Most of the photos have been taken down, leaving pale squares on the cork. A few remain, curling at the edges. One of them is you, two years younger, smiling for an ID camera. Beside your photo there is a gap. The name label under it still reads DR. E. CARTER.
actions.afterText: Your old photo, and the empty space beside it labelled DR. E. CARTER.

exits.label: Main corridor
exits.lockedText: You take one step into the corridor and stop. It is completely black in there. You would need a light. Your flashlight is in the patrol car’s glovebox.

security_office.name: Security office

description.text: A cramped room. A bank of dead monitors covers the wall ahead. A desk with a logbook sits on your left. On your right, a grey breaker panel labelled EMERGENCY POWER, and beside it a row of staff lockers.
The monitors ahead glow with nothing but static. Red emergency light falls across the desk and logbook on your left. The breaker panel on your right hums. Beside it, the row of staff lockers.

security_office.revisit: The security office. Monitors ahead, logbook on the left, breaker panel and lockers on the right.

text.text: Silence, mostly. The building settling. Your own breathing.
The breaker panel hums steadily on your right. The monitors whisper static.

details.text: And under it all, so soft you nearly miss it: a tiny electronic chirp, every few seconds, from low down among the lockers on your right. A low-battery warning.

actions.label: Read the logbook
actions.text: The last pages are still legible.
actions.afterText: The last logbook entries are in your journal.

text.text: A dozen dead screens. Your flashlight shows your own reflection in each one.
Every screen shows static. One, bottom left, flickers for a moment into a grey image of a long corridor, then back to noise. The label under it reads SUBLEVEL.
A heavy lever marked EMERGENCY POWER, currently down, and a row of smaller switches for each floor. The surface switch is labelled; the sublevel switches have been taped over.
The main lever is up and the panel hums. The sublevel switches are still taped over.

actions.label: Pull the emergency power lever
actions.text: You put your weight on the lever. It resists, then slams up. Somewhere deep in the walls, something heavy turns over. A rising whine. Then, one by one, red emergency lights come on along the ceiling.

text.text: A row of dented grey lockers, most hanging open and empty.
A row of dented grey lockers. The chirping is coming from the bottom one at the end. It is still shut, and dented as if someone kicked it closed.
A row of dented grey lockers, all open now.

actions.label: Force open the bottom locker
actions.text: You wedge your fingers into the bent door and pull until it screeches open. Inside: a dead walkie-talkie, still chirping its battery warning, and taped to the back wall, a red keycard with a folded note.

main_corridor.name: Main corridor

description.text: Your flashlight beam runs down a long corridor and does not find the end. Doors on either side. A noticeboard on your right. On your left, a door with a scraped nameplate. At the far end, the steel doors of an elevator, and beside them a stairwell door wrapped in chain. High on the wall above you, a speaker grille.

Emergency lights run the length of the corridor in a dotted red line. The noticeboard is on your right, the office with the scraped nameplate on your left. At the far end, the elevator, and the chained stairwell door. The speaker grille above you has a small green light now.

main_corridor.revisit: The main corridor. Office on the left, noticeboard on the right, elevator ahead, lobby behind.

listen.text: The corridor swallows sound. Your footsteps come back to you late. And far below your feet, so faint it could be your imagination, something mechanical shifts. Stops. Shifts again.

actions.label: Read the memo pinned on top
actions.text: One memo has been pinned over all the others, with four pins instead of one.
actions.afterText: The memo is in your journal.

text.text: A public address speaker, dead and dusty.
A public address speaker with a small green light. It is on. Someone could be listening through it, too.
A call button and a card reader. Both dead. There is no power.
The panel is lit, but the card reader blinks red: RESTRICTED. AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED.
The card reader glows green. The elevator is ready.

actions.label: Swipe the red override card
actions.text: You swipe the red card. The reader thinks about it for a long second, then chimes and turns green. Behind the steel doors, cables begin to move.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: A heavy new chain through both handles, and a padlock with a plastic tag: PROPERTY OF THE PROJECT BOARD. DO NOT REMOVE.

actions.label: Cut the chain with the bolt cutters
actions.text: You set the jaws on a link and lean on the handles until your arms shake. The link bites, then snaps with a crack that echoes down the whole corridor. The chain slithers to the floor.

lockedText.text: You press the call button. Nothing. The elevator has no power.
You press the call button. The card reader blinks red: RESTRICTED. AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED. You need clearance, or someone who can give it.

exits.label: Chained stairwell door
exits.lockedText: The chain is heavy and new, much newer than anything else here. It is not coming off without tools you do not have.

robotics_office.name: Robotics director’s office
robotics_office.description: A corner office that someone once loved. Shelves of mechanical parts and books. A desk ahead with a stack of papers and an old answering machine. A framed photo on the shelf to your left. On your right, a whiteboard covered in sketches of a hand: joints, tendons, a hundred small corrections.
robotics_office.revisit: The robotics director’s office. Desk ahead, photo on the left, whiteboard on the right.

listen.text: It is quieter in here than in the corridor, as if the room is holding its breath. On the desk, the answering machine has a faint electrical whine. It still has power from somewhere.

actions.label: Read the papers
actions.text: Under the dust, a bound document with a coffee ring on the cover.
actions.afterText: The project proposal is in your journal.

actions.label: Play the message
actions.text: A click, a whir, and a woman’s voice, quick and quiet, as if she is afraid of being overheard.
actions.afterText: The tape is saved in your journal. The machine clicks and waits.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: Two people at a robotics expo, laughing at something out of frame. A man in his forties with ink on his fingers, and a woman wearing a lanyard: DR. E. CARTER. Between them on the table, a robotic hand, posed mid-wave.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: Sketches of a hand, over and over, each one gentler than the last. In the corner, a number circled twice: 001.

actions.label: Look behind the whiteboard
actions.text: You tilt the board away from the wall. On the back, in the same careful handwriting: “001. First of its kind. Teach it kindness before anything else.” Below, in a different hand, harder and slanted: “Kindness is not a requirement.”
actions.afterText: “Teach it kindness before anything else.” And below it: “Kindness is not a requirement.”

elevator_car.name: Elevator
elevator_car.description: You step into the elevator. The doors slide shut behind you. There is only one button that is not taped over. It is marked B1.

b1_landing.name: Sublevel 1, elevator landing
b1_landing.description: The elevator doors open onto a low concrete landing. The air is cold and smells of disinfectant, with something sweeter underneath. Strips of emergency light run along the floor. Painted signs: LABORATORIES straight ahead. MEDICAL WARD on your right. STORAGE on your left. The elevator is behind you.
b1_landing.revisit: The elevator landing. Laboratories ahead, medical ward on the right, storage on the left.

details.text: The medical ward door on your right is shut. The panel beside it is dark.
The medical ward door on your right stands open. Its panel glows green.

listen.text: A deep ventilation drone, slow, like breathing. From straight ahead, down the laboratory corridor, a faint, regular electronic beep.

text.text: A dead keypad and, below it, an empty slot shaped for a portable power cell. A label: WARD EMERGENCY SUPPLY. INSERT CELL.
The panel glows green. A power cell sits in the emergency slot.

actions.label: Insert a power cell
actions.text: The cell slides in with a click. The panel lights, the lock thunks, and the ward door grinds open. Inside, machines begin to wake.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: The call panel by the elevator doors. The car is waiting here, doors open, but the surface button inside does nothing.

actions.label: Hold the door-open and B1 buttons together
actions.text: You step inside and hold both buttons down. One second. Three. Five. The panel blinks, clicks, and the surface button lights up.

exits.label: Elevator
exits.lockedText: You press the call button. Nothing. The car will only come down; the emergency circuit you restored does not reach the surface call buttons.

exits.label: Laboratory corridor
exits.lockedText: A steel security shutter has come down across the corridor, floor to ceiling. You hit it with your fist. Somewhere on the other side, Sarah is hitting it too.

exits.label: Medical ward
exits.lockedText: The medical ward door is sealed. The panel beside it is dark. There is an empty slot for a power cell.

exits.label: Elevator up to the surface
exits.text: The car climbs. The red lights of the surface floor slide down into view.

lab_corridor.name: Laboratory corridor
lab_corridor.description: Glass-walled laboratories line both sides, most of them dark and empty. One wall of glass on your right has been smashed outward and lies across the floor. On your left, a door marked TRANSFER SUITE. Straight ahead, the corridor ends at a heavy insulated door: PRESERVATION. A speaker grille hangs above you.
lab_corridor.revisit: The laboratory corridor. Transfer suite on the left, preservation lab ahead, the landing behind.

listen.text: Glass shifts under your boots. Ahead, through the heavy door, a slow electronic beep, about once a second. A heart monitor.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: The glass was broken from inside the lab, outward into the corridor. Whatever did it was strong. Inside the lab, nothing but an empty workbench and a chair on its side.

transfer_suite.name: Transfer suite
transfer_suite.description: A clean, white room that has not been cleaned in a long time. In the centre, a reclined chair with straps at the wrists, the ankles and the forehead. Behind it, racks of equipment cabled into the ceiling. On a trolley to your right, a portable recorder. On your left, a workbench and a sealed metal case.
transfer_suite.revisit: The transfer suite. The chair in the centre, recorder on the right, workbench and case on the left.

listen.text: The equipment racks tick as they cool, though nothing should be warm in here. A faint electrical crackle comes and goes, like a connection being tried and failing.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: The straps are worn pale where someone pulled against them. On the right armrest, scratched into the vinyl again and again, as if with a fingernail: I DID NOT AGREE.

actions.label: Play the recording
actions.text: You press play. Two voices, close to the microphone. A third sound under them: someone breathing hard against a strap.
actions.afterText: The transcript is in your journal. You do not want to hear it again.

text.text: Tools, cable ties, a coffee cup furred with mould. At the back, still in its charger, a portable power cell. Its light is green.
Tools, cable ties, a coffee cup furred with mould, and an empty charger.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: A heavy case with two latches. One latch is broken.

actions.label: Work the broken latch open
actions.text: It takes a while. When the lid finally lifts, there is only grey foam inside, cut to hold something small and rectangular. Whatever it was, it is gone. A label is stuck inside the lid.
actions.afterText: Empty foam, and the label: TRANSFER. SECONDARY. The destination has been scratched out.

description.text: Cold hits you like a wall. Your breath clouds. Along the wall on your right stands a row of tall glass capsules, frosted white. All of them are dark except one. That one glows a faint blue, and behind the frost there is a shape. On your left, a terminal screen glows.
The cold room. Emily’s capsule glows blue on your right, its monitor beeping. The terminal glows on your left.
The cold room. The row of capsules on your right, one of them empty now. The terminal glows on your left.

text.text: Only the hiss of the cooling system. Nothing else.
A slow, steady beep from the glowing capsule on your right. Under it, the hiss of cold air. And something else: very faint, almost lost, the sound of someone breathing.
Emily’s monitor beeps on your right. Her breathing is faint, but it is there.
The hiss of the cooling system around an empty capsule.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: You wipe the frost from the glass with your sleeve. A woman lies inside, eyes closed, her hair pale with frost. The monitor above her beeps, slow, steady. A label on the capsule frame: CARTER, E. She is alive.

afterText.text: Emily lies still behind the glass. The monitor is silent.
Emily Carter, asleep behind the glass. The capsule hums. The monitor beeps, slow and steady.

actions.label: Read the capsule status panel
actions.text: A small display on the capsule frame:

actions.label: Insert a power cell into the capsule
actions.text: You slot the cell into the capsule’s backup bay. The blue glow brightens a little.

actions.label: Release the floor clamps
actions.text: You find the release lever at the capsule’s base and pull. Four clamps let go of the floor with a bang. The capsule rocks on its wheeled cradle. It can be moved now, but only somewhere with power to plug it into: the medical ward.

actions.label: Wheel the capsule to the medical ward
actions.text: You put your shoulder to the cradle. It moves, heavy and slow, out through the insulated door, down the corridor, glass crunching under its wheels, across the landing and into the ward. The monitor beeps the whole way. In the life support bay, you line the capsule up with the dock and push it home. Cables find their sockets. The ward takes over.

actions.label: Read the records
actions.text: Most of the files are locked. One log is open, as if the last person here had been reading it.
actions.afterText: The preservation log is in your journal.

actions.label: Send the open records to Daniel
actions.text: You find the transfer option and pick the facility network. A progress bar crawls across the screen, then fills. Sent.

medical_ward.name: Medical ward
medical_ward.description: Rows of beds under plastic sheets. On your right, a life support bay with a docking cradle and a tangle of cables. On your left, a wall power bay with three slots. Ahead, a large status display.
medical_ward.revisit: The medical ward. Life support bay on the right, power bay on the left, display ahead.

details.text: Emily’s capsule is docked in the life support bay, its blue glow steady.
The life support bay is silent.

text.text: The soft pump of life support on your right, and Emily’s monitor beeping in time with it.
The hum of machines with nothing to do.

details.text: Paper flutters somewhere in the rows of beds, caught in the draft from a vent. Something has been left under one of the sheets.

text.text: You read the ward’s instructions taped to the bay and work through them slowly: oxygen mix, temperature, fluids. You wipe the frost from the glass. Her face is calm. Under your hand, the capsule is cold. The monitor’s rhythm evens out.
You go through the checks again: oxygen, temperature, fluids. Her breathing is steady. You stay a moment longer than you need to.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: Emily lies still behind the frosted glass. The monitor shows a flat line. You were too late.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: Three slots for portable power cells. Whatever is in them feeds the life support bay.

actions.label: Insert a power cell
actions.text: The cell clicks into a slot. The ward’s hum rises a little.

text.text: The display shows one occupied bay.
The display shows every bay empty.

actions.label: Read the clipboard
actions.text: You lift the sheet. A clipboard, its pages soft with damp.
actions.afterText: The revival protocol is in your journal.

actions.label: Patch yourself up
actions.text: You find bandages, a cold pack and painkillers, and do what you can for your side. It still hurts to breathe deeply, but you can move properly again.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: A glass-fronted cabinet: bandages, splints, cold packs, painkillers. Enough to patch up someone who has been hurt.

actions.label: Enter the revival codes
actions.text: You type the codes one by one, checking each twice. The capsule thinks about it. Then it hisses. The frost on the glass turns to water and runs down in lines, and the lid unseals with a sigh.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: A small panel on the capsule frame: REVIVAL. ENTER AUTHORIZATION CODES.

description.text: Metal shelving to the ceiling, crowded with crates and parts. On your right, a charging rack with a few portable power cells. And in the middle of the floor ahead of you, standing on a low crate, something tall under a grey tarp.

Metal shelving to the ceiling. The charging rack on your right. Ahead, on its crate, Prototype 001 stands docked and still, whining softly as it charges. On your left, behind the shelves, the freight lift.
Metal shelving to the ceiling. The charging rack on your right. Ahead, the empty crate where 001 stood, its grey tarp in a heap on the floor. On your left, behind the shelves, the freight lift.

revisit.text: Storage. The charging rack on the right, the shape under the tarp ahead.
Storage. 001 is docked ahead, charging. The freight lift on your left.
Storage. The empty crate ahead, the charging rack on the right, the freight lift on your left.

text.text: The charging rack clicks softly on your right. The shape under the tarp makes no sound at all. No fan, no hum, no standby tone. Complete silence, which is somehow worse.
The rising whine of 001 charging, straight ahead. Under it, very softly, a heartbeat: three short, one long.
The charging rack clicks softly on your right. The crate ahead is empty and silent.
Most slots are empty or dead. Two cells still show a green light.
Every slot is empty or dead now.

actions.label: Lift the edge of the tarp

text.text: The shape is roughly human, and taller than you. You lift one corner of the tarp. A hand. Mechanical, beautifully made, the fingers half curled as if about to hold something. It does not move. No light, no hum. Stencilled on the crate beneath it: PROTOTYPE 001. DO NOT ACTIVATE. BOARD ORDER.
The mechanical hand, fingers half curled. PROTOTYPE 001. DO NOT ACTIVATE. It has not moved.

actions.label: Wake Prototype 001
actions.text: You pull the tarp away. It slides to the floor with a sigh. You put your palm flat against 001’s chest plate, the way Daniel said. It is cold. Then, under your hand, it is not. Something deep inside it turns over, and a sound comes out of its chest, soft and clear: three short tones, and one long one.

actions.label: Listen to its chest
actions.text: You lean close. Under the charging whine, very softly, its heartbeat: three short, one long.

actions.label: Reach into its back panel for the key
actions.text: You ease the back panel open. It does not stir. Inside, clipped beside a coil of cable, a heavy metal key on a tag. You slide it free and close the panel. The charging whine does not change.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: A heavy cage lift behind the shelving, big enough for machinery. One key slot, stamped: 001 ONLY. Below it, a single destination: SUBLEVEL 2.

actions.label: Use 001’s key and ride the lift down

endChapter.title: End of Chapter 3
endChapter.text: The key turns. The cage shudders, and drops. The lights of Sublevel 1 slide away above you, and with them the slow, heavy footsteps. The air turns warmer as you go down, and it smells of machines that have never been switched off. Daniel’s voice comes through the lift speaker, very quietly: Sublevel 2. Whatever you see down here, remember what I wanted to build.

actions.label: Search the tool crate
actions.text: Spanners, cable, a dead drill. And at the bottom, heavy and long-handled, a pair of bolt cutters.

actions.label: Install 001’s original core
actions.text: You open its back panel again. Beside the empty key clip, a slot the same size as the amber core. You slide the core in until it clicks. The charging whine stops. Every light on 001 goes out.

exits.label: Freight lift down to Sublevel 2
exits.text: You turn 001’s key. The cage drops.

b2_lift.name: Sublevel 2, freight lift
b2_lift.description: The lift cage opens onto a wide concrete bay. It is warm down here, almost humid, and the air tastes of hot metal. Machines are running somewhere, and from the sound of them they have never once been switched off. A hall leads straight ahead.
b2_lift.revisit: The freight lift bay. The hall ahead, the lift up to storage behind you.

listen.text: A deep, even hum from every direction. Pumps. Fans. And, faint and slow, something that might be a ventilator, breathing for someone.

exits.label: Freight lift up to storage
exits.text: You turn 001’s key. The cage shudders upward.

b2_hall.name: Sublevel 2, main hall
b2_hall.description: A long hall with clean walls and good lighting, as if this floor was never abandoned at all. On your left, a door marked RECORDS. On your right, a glass room full of screens: MONITORING. Straight ahead, a heavy pressure door with a small window, stencilled CONTAINMENT.
b2_hall.revisit: The main hall. Records on the left, monitoring on the right, containment ahead.

listen.text: The hum is louder straight ahead, behind the containment door, and under it, slow and mechanical, the ventilator. In and out. In and out.

records_room.name: Records room
records_room.description: Rows of grey filing cabinets, and a reading table under a lamp that is still on. On the table, a folder left open. Against the far wall on your right, a steel archive shelf with numbered boxes.
records_room.revisit: The records room. Filing cabinets, the reading table ahead, the archive shelf on your right.

listen.text: Paper and silence. The lamp buzzes.

details.text: And from the archive shelf on your right, very faint, an electronic hum that does not belong to paper. Something in one of the boxes is still powered.

actions.label: Read the folder
actions.text: Board minutes. Someone was reading them recently enough that the lamp is still on.
actions.afterText: The board minutes are in your journal.

actions.label: Search for Emily’s file
actions.text: You go drawer by drawer. C. CARTER, E. Inside her file, an envelope marked REVIVAL, CAPSULE 3. Inside that, a printed sheet of codes.
actions.afterText: You already have the revival codes.

actions.label: Open the box
actions.text: Box 001. Inside, nested in foam, a small rectangular core module with a status light pulsing amber, the same amber 001’s eyes were before they turned white. The label: 001. ORIGINAL BEHAVIOURAL LAYER. ARCHIVED.
actions.afterText: The empty foam of box 001.

actions.label: Read the papers inside
actions.text: You had not noticed the safe before, behind the filing cabinets. Its door is open a crack, as if someone left in a hurry.
actions.afterText: The isolation order is in your journal.

monitoring.name: Monitoring station
monitoring.description: A glass room walled with screens. Most show empty corridors. One, on your left, shows a dot labelled 001 moving slowly across a floor plan of Sublevel 1. Ahead, a desk with a terminal marked MEDICAL LINK: WARD 1.
monitoring.revisit: Monitoring. The medical link terminal ahead, the floor plan screen on the left.

listen.text: Cooling fans, and the soft tick of screens refreshing.

text.text: A floor plan of Sublevel 1. A small dot labelled 001 walks its rounds: landing, corridor, labs, ward, storage. It never varies.
A floor plan of Sublevel 1. Nothing moves on it.

actions.label: Route Sublevel 2 power to the ward
actions.text: You find the ward on the power map and drag a line from Sublevel 2’s supply to it. The screen asks twice whether you are sure. You are.

effects.say: Emily’s ward now draws power from Sublevel 2. Her power will hold on its own.

actions.label: Run a remote check on Emily
actions.text: You walk the ward’s machines through their checks from here: oxygen, temperature, fluids. It helps, but a screen cannot do what hands can.

containment.name: Containment
containment.description: A sealed white room, warmer than anywhere else. In the centre, under a glass canopy, a medical bed surrounded by machines. Someone is lying in it. A ventilator breathes for them, slow and steady. On your left, a chart on a clipboard. On your right, against the wall, a tall empty frame with clamps for something the size of a person.
containment.revisit: Containment. The bed under its canopy ahead, the chart on the left, the empty frame on the right.

listen.text: The ventilator, in and out. A heart monitor, slower and lower than Emily’s. Nothing else. No movement from the bed. There has not been any for a long time.

actions.label: Look through the canopy
actions.text: A man in his forties, thinner than he should be, his hair grown long. Tubes, wires, a ventilator mask. His eyes are closed. His hands lie on the sheet, and there is still ink on his fingers, faded almost to nothing. You know this face from the photo in his office. It is Daniel.
actions.afterText: Daniel’s body, breathing because a machine tells it to.

actions.label: Read the chart
actions.text: Neat, clinical handwriting, updated every day for a very long time. The last entry is recent.
actions.afterText: The chart is in your journal.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: A standing cradle of steel and cable, built to hold a body upright: not a human one. The clamps are open. Whatever stood here is gone. A plate on the frame: TRANSFER RECIPIENT. Under it, a strip of tape with one word written in marker: RELOCATED.

stairwell.name: East stairwell
stairwell.description: Concrete stairs going down into the dark, between the surface and Sublevel 1. Your flashlight finds footprints in the dust on every step, going down and coming back up. Some of them are fresh. Halfway down, on a landing, a heavy steel door with a keypad. Stencilled on it: ISOLATION.
stairwell.revisit: The east stairwell. The isolation door on the landing below, the corridor behind you.

listen.text: Your own breathing, loud in the stairwell. From behind the isolation door, a soft, steady whir. You have heard that whir before, on the other end of the radio, every time Daniel went quiet.

details.text: And under the whir, very faintly, someone humming. A slow tune you do not know. Then it stops, as if it has heard you.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: Two sets. One set is old and blurred, many trips over a long time. The other is sharp and recent: hard-soled shoes, someone who walked down to the isolation door, stood there a while, and walked back up. Not tonight. But not long ago.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: Steel, cold, and very thick. A keypad with a single button marked ENTER, and a small speaker grille. The keypad does not want numbers: its label says RHYTHM CODE.

actions.label: Knock on the door
actions.text: You knock. The whir behind the door stops. Nothing answers. After a long moment, the whir starts again.

actions.label: Tap the signal on the keypad: three short, one long

exits.label: Back up to the main corridor

isolation.name: Isolation
isolation.description: A small dark room inside the stairwell wall. Cables hang from the ceiling. Against the far wall, held upright by clamps at the wrists, the chest and the throat, stands Daniel: tall, steel and grey composite, a face built to look gentle. His amber eyes follow you.
isolation.revisit: Isolation. Daniel, clamped to the far wall, watching you.

listen.text: The soft whir of Daniel’s body, close enough to touch. When he is not speaking, it slows, like breathing. Somewhere inside his chest, very faint: three short, one long.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: Heavy steel, bolted through the wall. No keyhole, no release lever. A small receiver on each clamp, with a red light. They answer to a remote, and you do not have it.

actions.label: Tell Daniel you are ready to decide

apartment.name: Your apartment

description.text: Your small apartment smells of garlic and something burning slightly. Emily is at the stove on your left, laughing at Daniel, who is setting your table on the right with great care and too many forks. On the kitchen table ahead, where you always keep it, the old facility radio. By the front door behind you, your coat.

Your small apartment. On your right, 001 is standing at your stove, stirring a pot with enormous care, the way it does everything now. When it speaks, it speaks with Daniel’s voice. On the kitchen table ahead, the old facility radio. The front door is behind you.

Your small apartment, quiet except for the fridge. A TV on your left. On the kitchen table ahead, where you always keep it, the old facility radio. You have never been able to throw it away. The front door is behind you.

apartment.revisit: Your apartment. The radio on the table ahead, the front door behind you.

text.text: Two voices, laughing at the stove. A pan sizzling. Rain on the window.
A wooden spoon on a pot, slow and careful. A soft whir. Rain on the window.
The fridge hums. Rain on the window. Your own breathing.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: The handheld radio from the reception desk, months ago. The battery should have died long ago. Its little light is on.

text.text: News anchor: Police are investigating the death of Dr. Alan Pryce, a former director of a private research company, found at his home tonight. He is the fourth former board member of the company to die this year. Police are not commenting on a possible connection.

News anchor: Police are investigating the death of Dr. Alan Pryce, a former director of a private research company, found at his home tonight. A source close to the investigation says a police radio was found at the scene.

exits.label: Front door
exits.lockedText: You reach for the handle, and someone on the other side knocks first. Three hard knocks.

interview_room.name: Interview room, police station
interview_room.description: A grey room you have sat in a hundred times, always on the other side of the table. A metal table ahead, bolted down. A long mirror on your left that is not a mirror. The camera light in the corner is red.
interview_room.revisit: The interview room. The table ahead, the mirror on your left.

listen.text: Fluorescent lights buzzing. Through the door, phones ringing and people you used to work with, talking quietly about you.

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: Your own face, tired. Somewhere behind it, people are watching you the way you used to watch suspects.

holding_cell.name: Holding cell
holding_cell.description: A narrow cell. A steel cot on your right. Bars ahead, and a corridor light beyond them. On your left, low on the wall, an air vent.
holding_cell.revisit: The holding cell. The cot on the right, the vent on the left, the bars ahead.

listen.text: A tap drips somewhere down the corridor. A drunk two cells over is singing to himself.

details.text: And from the vent on your left, very faintly, someone tapping on a pipe. Three short. One long.

actions.label: Put your ear to the vent
Sit down
actions.text: The steel is cold through your clothes. You think about everyone you ever put in a cell like this, and wonder how many of them were telling the truth.

street.name: Downtown, in the rain
street.description: A wet downtown street, morning traffic hissing past. Ahead, the stairs up to your lawyer’s office. On your right, a small cafe with steamed-up windows. On your left, the all-night diner where the facility’s old night shift still gathers. Behind you, the way home.
street.revisit: The street. The lawyer’s office ahead, the cafe on the right, the diner on the left, home behind you.

listen.text: Tyres on wet tarmac. A bus sighing at its stop. Somebody’s radio in a parked car, and for a horrible second you listen for three short, one long. It is only music.

okafor_office.name: Okafor’s office
okafor_office.description: A cramped office above a laundromat. Files stacked on every surface. Nadia Okafor sits behind a desk ahead, reading glasses pushed up into her hair.
okafor_office.revisit: Okafor’s office. Okafor at her desk ahead.

listen.text: The laundromat below rumbles. Okafor’s pen scratches. She is humming, slightly off key.

cafe.name: Cafe

description.text: Warm, loud, smelling of coffee. Every table is taken except one by the window, where a woman with a laptop is sitting. As you come in, she looks up, straight at you, as if she has been waiting.
Warm, loud, smelling of coffee. Sarah’s table by the window, her laptop open.

cafe.revisit: The cafe. Sarah’s table by the window.

listen.text: The espresso machine screaming. Cups. Somebody laughing. And from the window table, a laptop fan, and very soft keyboard clicks.

diner.name: Night shift diner
diner.description: Red booths and bad coffee. The facility closed two years ago, but its night shift never stopped coming here. In a booth on your left, Ana from accounts. At the counter ahead, Theo, the old night security guard. In the corner on your right, Priya from the labs, pretending not to see you.
diner.revisit: The diner. Ana on the left, Theo at the counter ahead, Priya in the corner on the right.

listen.text: A grill hissing. A jukebox nobody fed. Three conversations go quiet when you walk in, and then, slowly, start again.

description.text: Emily and Daniel’s flat, full of books and half-built machines. Emily is at the kitchen table ahead. Daniel is in the armchair on your right, his cane against the wall.
Emily’s flat, full of books and half-built machines. Emily is at the kitchen table ahead.

listen.text: A kettle starting to sing. Rain on the skylight.

county_jail.name: County jail, visiting room
county_jail.description: A long table divided by glass. On the other side, in an orange jumpsuit that makes him look even older, Marcus Hale.
county_jail.revisit: The visiting room. Marcus behind the glass.

listen.text: A buzzer. Keys. Marcus breathing on the other side of the glass.

courtroom.name: Courtroom 4
courtroom.description: Wood panelling and bad air conditioning. The judge’s bench ahead, high and far away. The jury box on your right: twelve strangers deciding the rest of your life. The prosecutor’s table on your left. Behind you, the gallery, and every face you persuaded to come.
courtroom.revisit: Courtroom 4. The judge ahead, the jury on your right, the prosecution on your left, your people behind you.

listen.text: Paper. Coughs. The air conditioning rattling. Twelve people breathing on your right. And somewhere in the walls, very faint, a speaker system hissing as if it is waiting for something.

court_hallway.name: Courthouse hallway
court_hallway.description: A long marble hallway outside Courtroom 4, echoing with footsteps and whispered phone calls. Sarah sits on a bench on your left with her laptop. Okafor paces ahead, near a vending machine. The courtroom doors are behind you.
court_hallway.revisit: The hallway. Sarah on the bench on your left, Okafor ahead, the courtroom behind you.

listen.text: Heels on marble. A vending machine humming. Sarah’s keyboard, fast. And below the floor, a lift motor running when no lift has been called.

evidence_room.name: Courthouse evidence room
evidence_room.description: A windowless basement room of steel shelves and numbered boxes. Ruiz stands by the door on your left. Sarah is ahead of you at an old terminal on a desk, the kind nobody has used in years, with a speaker on top and a cable running into the wall. Its screen is on. On a shelf on your right, in a clear evidence bag: your radio.
evidence_room.revisit: The evidence room. Ruiz by the door on your left, Sarah and the terminal ahead, your radio on the shelf on your right.

listen.text: Fluorescent tubes buzzing. The terminal’s fan. And inside its speaker, very quietly, something breathing that does not need to breathe.

objects.name: Your old radio, in an evidence bag

actions.label: Examine
actions.text: Your police radio, the one you handed in after the facility call. Someone has opened the back and soldered a small board inside, with a cable that would fit the terminal. Its little light blinks: three short, one long.

switching_room.name: Switching room
switching_room.description: A narrow room behind monitoring, packed floor to ceiling with racks of old telephone switching gear, relays clicking like insects. Ahead, a master panel with a big red isolation lever and a smaller labelled breaker. Every speaker grille in the room is turned toward you.
switching_room.revisit: The switching room. The master panel ahead.

listen.text: Thousands of relays, clicking and settling, clicking and settling. Under it, a breath that has nowhere to come from. She is all around you.

police_radio.name: Police radio
police_radio.description: Your shoulder radio, tuned to dispatch. Your call sign is Unit 14.

flashlight.name: Flashlight
flashlight.description: A heavy police-issue flashlight. Fresh batteries.

facility_radio.name: Facility radio
facility_radio.description: A handheld radio from the facility’s own system. Someone inside the building is on the other end.

override_card.name: Red override card
override_card.description: A red maintenance keycard. Printed on the back: OVERRIDE. NOT FOR ROUTINE USE.

power_cell_a.name: Power cell
power_cell_a.description: A heavy portable power cell, the kind the facility uses for emergency equipment. Charged.

power_cell_b.name: Power cell
power_cell_b.description: A heavy portable power cell, the kind the facility uses for emergency equipment. Charged.

power_cell_c.name: Power cell
power_cell_c.description: A heavy portable power cell, the kind the facility uses for emergency equipment. Charged.

key_001.name: 001’s key
key_001.description: A heavy metal key on a tag stamped 001. It opens the freight lift to Sublevel 2.

revival_codes.name: Revival codes
revival_codes.description: A printed sheet of authorization codes for Capsule 3. Enter them on the revival panel of Emily’s capsule in the medical ward.

core_001.name: 001’s original core
core_001.description: A small core module, its light pulsing amber. 001’s original behavioural layer: the one Daniel wrote.

bolt_cutters.name: Bolt cutters
bolt_cutters.description: Heavy, long-handled bolt cutters from the storage tool crate.

emily_badge.name: Emily’s lanyard
emily_badge.description: Her old staff lanyard, the one she wears in the photo in Daniel’s office. DR. E. CARTER. ROBOTICS. She asked you to give it to Daniel.

marcus_remote.name: Marcus’s remote
marcus_remote.description: A small black remote. One button opens Daniel’s clamps. The red one switches him off, for good.

doc_dispatch_notes.title: Dispatch call notes
text: Call received 7:52 PM. Repeating signal on emergency band, source triangulated to the research facility on the north road. Pattern: three short tones, one long. No voice. No response to hails.
Facility listed as closed. No keyholder on file.
Unit 14 to respond and investigate. Your own handwriting underneath, pressed hard into the paper: You know this place.

doc_visitor_log.title: Visitor log
text: Most of the page is water-damaged. The last legible entries:
Board delegation, six visitors. Signed in 9:10 AM. Signed out 6:45 PM.
Technician, contractor badge. Signed in 11:30 AM. Signed out 4:05 PM.
Dr. E. Carter. Signed in 8:40 PM. Reason for visit: Meeting, Robotics. Signed out: blank.
There are no entries after that one.

doc_directory.title: Building directory
text: Ground floor: Reception. Security. Administration. Robotics Division, Director’s Office.
Sublevel 1: Laboratories. Medical Ward. Storage.
Sublevel 2: Restricted. Authorized personnel only.
Someone has peeled the letters off the Sublevel 2 line and pressed them back on in the wrong order.

doc_security_log.title: Security logbook, final entries
text: Board order: power to sublevels to be cut at the end of the night shift. Do not restore without written authorization.
Robotics director’s access revoked effective today. He is not to be admitted to the building. If he arrives, call the number on the board, not the police.
Noises from Sublevel 2 again. Told to log it and leave it.
Last entry, different handwriting, barely legible: They said everyone was out. Somebody is still talking on the radio.

doc_reassignment_memo.title: Memo from the Project Board
text: To all staff.
Effective immediately, the Director of Robotics is relieved of all duties. Ongoing work under his supervision is transferred to the Project Board.
Prototype 001 is to remain in storage, inactive, until further notice. No staff are to attempt activation.
Questions about these changes are not to be directed to the former director.

doc_proposal.title: Project proposal: a helpful humanoid assistant
text: Submitted by Daniel, Director of Robotics.

We have built machines that are strong and machines that are fast. I want to build one that is kind. A humanoid assistant that can help someone stand up after a fall, carry groceries up the stairs, sit with a patient through a long night, and know when to be quiet.
Everything in this design begins with the hands. A hand that can hold a cup without breaking it can also hold a hand.
A note in the margin, in different handwriting: Daniel, the hands section is beautiful. Do not let the board cut it. E.

doc_override_note.title: Note taped to the override card
text: For the elevator, if the board locks everyone out again. Do not tell them this exists.
If anyone asks, you never had it. M.

doc_preservation_log.title: Preservation log, Capsule 3
text: Occupant: Carter, E., Dr.
Reason for preservation: interference with a Project Board directive. Attempted access to sealed Sublevel 2 records.
Authorized by Board resolution. Revival: not authorized. Review date: left blank.
Capsule backup power: maintenance overdue. Maintenance overdue. Maintenance overdue.
Appended note: Transfer subject D. All records sealed at Sublevel 2.

doc_case_label.title: Label inside the metal case
text: TRANSFER. SECONDARY.
Destination: scratched out, hard enough to tear the label.
The foam is cut for something small and rectangular. It is empty.

doc_revival_protocol.title: Revival protocol, Capsule 3 (draft, unsigned)
text: Patient must be stabilized in the medical ward before any revival attempt.
Revival requires authorization codes held at Sublevel 2.
Expect confusion on waking. Speak calmly. Familiar voices help.
Someone has underlined the last line twice.

doc_001_tag.title: Tag on 001’s key
text: PROTOTYPE 001. Freight access, Sublevel 2.
Behavioural layer revised by order of the Project Board. Original layer archived, Sublevel 2.
Under the printed text, in small careful handwriting you have seen before: be gentle with it.

doc_board_minutes.title: Project Board minutes, Resolution 14
text: Resolution 14. The Director of Robotics has refused to cooperate with the continuation programme.
The Board authorizes transfer of the Director’s neural map to the recipient frame. Consent is not required, the Director being party to Board confidentiality terms.
The biological subject is to be maintained. Its continued existence is of value.
Dr. E. Carter is to be informed that the Director has taken leave. Should she persist, Preservation is approved.
Recipient frame: relocated after incident. Location restricted to Board members.

doc_revival_codes.title: Revival codes, Capsule 3
text: CAPSULE 3. CARTER, E. REVIVAL AUTHORIZATION.
A grid of letters and numbers. At the bottom, in pen: never to be used.

doc_body_chart.title: Containment chart, Patient D.
text: Patient D. Biological functions maintained artificially since the transfer.
Neural activity: none detected since transfer.
Maintain indefinitely. Board note: leverage.
The most recent entry is in different handwriting from all the others. It says only: still here.

doc_isolation_order.title: Isolation order
text: By order of the Project Board. Recipient frame to be relocated to Isolation, east stairwell, following the incident.
Restraints to remain engaged at all times. Network access limited to facility audio only.
Door code set to the subject’s own heartbeat pattern. Somebody on the Board thought that was funny.
Access from Sublevel 1: maintenance override on the elevator, door-open and B1 together, five seconds.

doc_padlock_tag.title: Tag on the stairwell padlock
text: PROPERTY OF THE PROJECT BOARD. DO NOT REMOVE.
On the back, a date in marker. It is less than a month old.

doc_p2_charge.title: Charge sheet
text: Charge: murder of Dr. Alan Pryce.
Arresting officer: Detective A. Ruiz.
Basis: physical evidence at the scene; anonymous information received 3:02 AM.

doc_p2_scene.title: Scene report, Pryce residence
text: Victim found in his study, 11:04 PM.
On the desk: a police-issue radio, playing a looping recording: three short tones, one long.
In the victim’s hand: a note bearing the badge number of the accused.
In the desk drawer: a page torn from a visitor log, bearing the accused’s name and the date of the facility call.
Note: the radio is the same model issued to the accused. The accused’s own radio was handed in after the facility call and logged into evidence. It is no longer in the evidence room.

rec_emily_voicemail.title: Answering machine tape
text: Woman’s voice: Daniel, it’s me. Pick up if you’re there. Something is wrong. They’ve moved your files downstairs, all of them, and nobody will tell me why.
I’m going to come in tonight and find out. Call me back. Please.
End of message.

rec_transfer_log.title: Recorder in the transfer suite
text: First voice: Board resolution fourteen is on file. Consent is not required.
Second voice: He’s awake. He’s asking for Emily.
First voice: Sedate him. Begin the transfer.
Second voice: Neural map at sixty percent. Eighty. The body’s heart rate is dropping.
First voice: Keep going. The body doesn’t matter now.
A long tone. Then the second voice, quieter: Transfer complete. Is it... is it talking?
First voice: Turn it off. Turn it off.
The recording ends.

find_signal.text: Find the source of the signal.

restore_power.text: Restore emergency power from the security office.

find_way_down.text: Find a way down to the lower levels.

retrieve_records.text: Find the records terminal in the preservation lab.

save_emily.text: Get Emily to the medical ward.

power_ward.text: Get power to the medical ward door. It takes a power cell.

keep_emily_alive.text: Keep Emily alive: check on her in the ward, and keep her power up with power cells.

wake_001.text: Wake Prototype 001 in the storage room.

get_key.text: Take the key from 001’s back panel while it recharges in storage. Listen for it.

ride_lift.text: Ride the freight lift in storage down to Sublevel 2.

find_daniel.text: Find what Daniel meant by what’s left of him. He said: containment.

find_codes.text: Find Emily’s revival codes in the records room on Sublevel 2.

wake_emily.text: Take the revival codes to the medical ward on Sublevel 1 and wake Emily.

find_isolation.text: Find out where the board put the rest of Daniel.

go_up.text: Get the elevator on Sublevel 1 to take you up to the surface.

get_cutters.text: Find something to cut the chain on the surface stairwell door. Storage might have tools.

meet_marcus.text: Someone has come in through the front gate. Meet them in reception.

p2_evening.text: A quiet evening at home. For once.

p2_night.text: Get through the night in the holding cell.

see_okafor.text: Go and see your lawyer, Okafor. Her office is up the stairs ahead of you on the street.

find_witnesses.text: Find people who will testify for you: try the diner, Emily, and anyone else who knew you. Then go back to Okafor.

recess.text: Recess. Talk to Sarah and Okafor in the hallway, then go back into the courtroom.

evidence_room.text: Go down to the courthouse evidence room with Sarah and Ruiz, and find the voice.

reach_switching.text: Get to the switching room behind monitoring on Sublevel 2: storage, then the freight lift down.

trust_radio.text: Voss can fake any voice through the speakers. The real Sarah is only on your radio.

open.speaker: daniel

lines.narration: The radio in your hand clicks. Someone on the other end has pressed transmit. You hear breathing that is almost, but not quite, right. Then a man’s voice, low and careful.

lines: You picked it up. Good. I was starting to think no one ever would.
Who sent you?

choices.text: Police. Dispatch picked up a signal from this place.

trust.reason: told the truth about being police

choices.text: I used to work here. A long time ago.

trust.reason: admitted they used to work here

choices.text: Just a maintenance contractor. Checking the power.

effects.say: You keep your thumb off the transmit button.

police.speaker: daniel
lines: Police. So someone finally heard it.
Fine. Better you than one of them.

former.speaker: daniel

lines.narration: A long pause. Long enough that you check the radio is still on.

lines: Then you know what this place is. Or you think you do.
You came back. Most people who leave here don’t.

contractor.speaker: daniel
lines: A contractor. At two in the morning. In the rain.
All right. Let’s say I believe you.

silence.speaker: daniel
lines: Careful. I understand careful.
But I can hear the rain on your coat, so don’t pretend you’re not there.

lines.text: There is a security office off the lobby. Emergency power. Turn it on and I won’t need this toy radio to talk to you.
You already turned the emergency power on. That’s how I found you. Keep the radio anyway.

who.speaker: daniel
lines: Someone who used to matter here.
Turn the power on. Then we’ll see how much I tell you.

why_trust.speaker: daniel
lines: You shouldn’t. I don’t trust you either.
That makes us even. It’s a place to start.

lines.narration: The channel clicks closed. The lobby is quiet again, except for the rain.

open.speaker: daniel

endChapter.title: Ending: Two Coffees
endChapter.text: Daniel opens his eyes in his own body, and the first thing he sees is Emily, asleep in the chair beside him with her hand on his. Weeks later, the doctors say he will walk again. Months later, he does. Every morning he brings two coffees, and one of them is never a mistake. She tells him, finally, the thing she came to say that night. He already knew. On the last night before the facility is sealed for good, the old facility radio on your kitchen table clicks on by itself. Three short tones. One long. Not his.

endChapter.title: Ending: Home
endChapter.text: Daniel wakes in his own body, weak and thin and himself. He can barely lift a cup. He laughs about it, and it is the first time you have heard him laugh. The facility is sealed. The board is investigated. His hands heal slowly. Some nights, he says, he still listens for the whir of a body that is not there anymore. One night months later, your phone rings from an unknown number. Three short tones. One long.

endChapter.title: Ending: Silence
endChapter.text: Daniel is gone. You stand in the dark room until the rain stops. Below you, a ventilator keeps breathing for a body that has nobody to come home to it. You walk out of the facility at dawn and do not look back, again. But for years afterward, whenever a radio crackles, you wait for three short tones and one long. They never come.

endChapter.title: Ending: Names
endChapter.text: He walks out of the stairwell, through the lobby, and out into the rain without looking back. You report the facility in the morning. Over the following year, one by one, the names on the Project Board stop answering their phones. Nobody can explain how. Every case file has the same strange detail: a recording found at the scene, three short tones and one long. You keep your own copy of the report in a drawer, and you never decide whether you did the right thing.

endChapter.title: Ending: The First of Its Kind
endChapter.text: The transfer is quiet. When it is done, the frame on the wall is empty, and 001 opens its amber eyes and says hello in Daniel’s voice, gentle and slightly too slow, like someone reading aloud for a child. The body that was built to hold a cup without breaking it holds yours, very carefully, and shakes it. It is the helper he always meant to build, and it has his mind, and his kindness, and nothing the board ever wrote. Some say the secret of the whole experiment was always in 001. They are right. Months later, three short tones and one long come over every police radio in the county. Then: Hello. I am here to help.
