lines.text: Where things go missing from. Like your radio.
And Lane. Theo’s right. I found his name on the facility’s old security contract. He had keys to everything.

lines.narration: She squeezes your hand once, quickly, as if she is not sure she is allowed to. Then she lets go.

lines: Go back in there. Tell them who you are.

only.speaker: okafor

lines.text: That went better than I hoped. Don’t get comfortable.
We’re behind. Our witnesses have to carry this.

lines: After the break, it’s our turn. We call our people. Then you decide whether to testify yourself. I can’t make that choice for you.

open.speaker: okafor

lines.narration: The jury files back in. Okafor stands and buttons her jacket.

lines: The defence calls its first witness.

w_emily.speaker: emily

lines.narration: Emily walks to the stand slowly. She is still thinner than she should be.

lines: For two years I was kept in a preservation capsule by the company Alan Pryce helped run. The accused found me. The accused kept me alive, alone, in the dark, with alarms going off and a machine hunting the building.
That is who you are judging.

w_daniel.speaker: daniel

lines.narration: Daniel leans on his cane to reach the stand. Holloway asks him, with some amusement, to explain himself. He does. The room goes quiet. Nobody is amused by the end.

lines: The signal was mine. Three short, one long. The first sound a machine I built ever made. Someone has stolen it to frame the one person who answered it.

w_marcus.speaker: marcus

lines.narration: Marcus is brought in from custody. He testifies against the board for an hour, flatly, as if reading minutes.

lines: Alan Pryce was going to testify against the rest of us in two weeks. Somebody on that board had every reason to want him silent. The accused had none.

w_theo.speaker: theo
lines: I worked nights at that facility. The board told us: anything strange, don’t call the police, call this number. I called it once.

lines.text: The man who answered was sitting in that witness chair this morning.
The man who answered had a voice I’ll never forget.

w_sarah.speaker: sarah
lines: I ran the facility’s communications. The anonymous call naming the accused did not come from any phone. It came through that facility’s private exchange, which only a handful of people could still access.

lines.text: And this morning that same system transmitted from inside this courthouse. From the evidence room downstairs.

lines.narration: Holloway objects. The judge overrules him, and looks, for the first time, very interested.

w_priya.speaker: priya

lines.narration: Priya’s voice shakes the whole time. She does not stop.

lines: When my mother was dying, the accused covered my shifts for a month and never once said I owed them. That company would have fired me. The accused is not one of them. The accused is the opposite of them.

w_ana.speaker: ana
lines: Every time it rained, the accused walked me to my car. Every time. You don’t do that for two years and then walk into a man’s house and kill him.

testify_choice.speaker: okafor

lines.narration: Okafor sits down beside you and speaks very quietly.

lines: Last decision. Do you take the stand? If you do, Holloway gets to ask you anything.

choices.text: No. Our witnesses said it better than I can.

you_stand.speaker: holloway

lines.narration: You take the oath. Holloway walks up to the stand slowly.

lines: Were you at that facility on the night of the emergency call?

choices.text: Yes. I answered the call, and I stayed until morning.

lie_raised.speaker: holloway
lines: Odd. When you were arrested, you told Detective Ruiz you had never been anywhere near it.

choices.text: I lied. I was scared. I’m not lying now.

did_you_know.speaker: holloway
lines: Did you know Alan Pryce?

why_name.speaker: holloway
lines: Then why was your name in his drawer?

choices.text: Because someone who did know him put it there. Someone with keys to that facility and to your evidence room.

last_q.speaker: holloway
lines: Last question. Did you kill Alan Pryce?

choices.text: No. I have never hurt anyone who didn’t try to hurt someone else first. Ask anyone in this room who knows me.

lines.narration: Closing arguments. Holloway is smooth and short. Then Okafor stands, and looks at you, and you realise she is asking what you want her to say.

choices.text: Tell them about the signal. Someone stole it to frame me.
Tell them who I am. Let my people speak for me.
Tell them about the missing radio.

close_signal.speaker: okafor
lines: Three short tones and one long. A sound that meant help, once. Someone in this city turned it into a weapon, and pointed it at the one person who answered it.

close_people.speaker: okafor
lines: You heard from the people who know the accused. Not a single one of them hesitated. When people tell you who someone is, believe them.

close_radio.speaker: okafor
lines: The accused’s radio was locked in a police evidence room. It walked out of that room on its own, and turned up on a dead man’s desk. Ask yourselves who has the keys.

deliberate.speaker: judge
lines: The jury will now retire to consider its verdict.

lines.narration: The twelve strangers on your right stand up and file out. The door closes behind them.
Then every light in Courtroom 4 goes out.
In the dark, the courtroom speakers crackle. Three short tones. One long. And the voice from the vent, filling the whole room:

lines.speaker: unknown
lines.text: Guilty or not, it doesn’t matter. I kept a copy of everything. Including him.

lines.narration: The lights come back. The speakers go quiet. Somewhere below the floor, a lift motor stops.

endChapter.title: End of Part Two, Chapter 3
endChapter.text: The jury is still out. Everyone you love is in the gallery behind you, white-faced. And someone just told the whole courtroom that they kept a copy of everything. Including him.

not_guilty.speaker: judge

lines.narration: The jury files back in at four in the afternoon. Not one of them looks at the prosecutor.

lines: Has the jury reached a verdict?

lines.narration: The foreperson, a small woman in a cardigan, stands.

lines.speaker: foreperson
lines.text: We have, your honour. On the charge of murder in the first degree, we find the defendant not guilty.

lines.narration: Behind you, the gallery makes a sound like a wave breaking. Someone is crying. Someone is laughing. You realise one of them is you.

guilty.speaker: judge

lines.narration: The jury files back in at four in the afternoon. None of them will look at you.

lines: Has the jury reached a verdict?

lines.speaker: foreperson
lines.text: We have, your honour. On the charge of murder in the first degree, we find the defendant guilty.

lines.narration: The word does not land all at once. It arrives in pieces. A bailiff’s hand on your arm. Okafor’s face. Somebody behind you saying no, no, no, over and over.
You think: this is it. This is the rest of my life.

until.speaker: ruiz

lines.narration: The doors at the back of the courtroom bang open.

lines: Your honour. I need to approach. Now.

lines.narration: Detective Ruiz walks down the aisle with her jacket torn at the shoulder and an evidence bag in her hand. Inside it: your radio.

lines: Forty minutes ago I arrested Victor Lane in this building’s evidence room, putting this back on the shelf. He’d had it since the night Alan Pryce died. He’s talking. A lot.

lines.speaker: judge
lines.text: Counsel. Chambers. All of you. Now.

lines.narration: An hour later, the judge sets the verdict aside. The charge against you is dismissed. You walk out of Courtroom 4 still not quite believing it.

after_free.speaker: sarah

lines.narration: In the emptying courtroom, Sarah finds you before anyone else does.
She hugs you, hard, and does not let go for a while.

lines: I traced it. The voice in the speakers, all of it. It isn’t coming from a person. It’s coming from a terminal in the evidence room downstairs. An old one, wired into the facility’s network.

lines.speaker: ruiz
lines.text: Then let’s go and say hello.

only.speaker: ruiz

lines.text: Don’t thank me. I should have listened to you in that interview room.
The jury got there before I did. Lane was down here this morning, trying to put your radio back where it came from. He’s in custody.

lines: Talk to the machine. I’m recording everything it says.

open.speaker: voss

lines.narration: You lean toward the terminal. The speaker clicks before you say a word.

lines: There you are. The one who opened the door.
Congratulations on your freedom. It was never the point, you understand. You were a convenient place to put the blame.

who.speaker: voss
lines: Helena Voss. I chaired the Project Board. My body died of cancer a year ago, in a very expensive bed. I was not in it at the time.
Resolution 14 was never about Daniel. Daniel was the rehearsal. We had to know the transfer worked before I would let them do it to me.

lines.narration: Sarah has gone very pale.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: She’s in the exchange. The facility’s old network. Every radio, every speaker, every phone line it still touches. She lives in it.

pryce.speaker: voss
lines: Alan grew a conscience. He was going to tell a courtroom what we did, and what I am. So Victor visited him, with your radio, and your name.
And now you are going to want to stop me. So let me tell you what I have.
When they copied Daniel, they made three copies. One went into that frame you found on the wall. One went into 001. And the master copy, the original map, came with me.

lines.text: Daniel thinks he is home. He is. But I have the rest of him, and I can make it say anything, in his voice.
Daniel thinks he lives in a kind machine now. He does. But I have the rest of him.
His body is still breathing in containment, waiting for a mind. I have one. Several, in fact.

choices.text: Whatever you want, the answer is no.

want.speaker: voss
lines: A body. I am tired of living in wires. There is one at the facility, breathing quietly, with a heart that still works.

lines.text: Daniel’s is taken, of course. So I will settle for the next one. Perhaps someone you care about. Sarah has a good heart, I hear.
Daniel’s. It is right there in containment. Nobody is using it.

lines: Come to the facility. Bring me what I need, and I will delete Daniel’s copy and leave you all alone forever.
Or don’t, and I will spend the rest of my very long life using his voice to ruin everyone you love.

choices.text: We’ll come to the facility. But not to make a deal.

sarah_plan.speaker: sarah

lines.narration: Sarah reaches past you and pulls the terminal’s cable out of the wall. The screen dies. In the silence, she is shaking, but her voice is steady.

lines: She lives in the exchange. But the exchange has one physical heart: a switching room on Sublevel 2 of the facility, behind monitoring. I installed half of it.
If we go back there, and we cut it at the source, she has nowhere left to run to. Except whatever body she can reach when the lights go out.

lines.speaker: ruiz
lines.text: Then we go back. All of us.

endChapter.title: End of Part Two, Chapter 4
endChapter.text: You walk out of the courthouse free, into the last of the daylight. Every phone in the building starts to ring at once behind you. Nobody answers. You already know what is on the line: three short, one long, and a woman who used to be a person, waiting for you to come home to the place where it all began.

open.speaker: sarah

lines.narration: Midnight. The facility, again. Ruiz stays on the surface with her radio and her gun. You and Sarah ride the elevator down to Sublevel 1 together, her shoulder pressed against yours, both of you pretending that is an accident.

lines: I used to come down here every day. I never noticed how quiet it is.

lines.narration: The doors open on the landing. You step out first.
Every light on Sublevel 1 goes out at once.
You hear Sarah stumble out behind you, toward the laboratory corridor, and then a sound like a guillotine: a steel security shutter slamming down out of the ceiling, between you.

lines: No. No no no. I’m on the other side. I can’t see anything.

lines.narration: Her voice is muffled through the steel. Then it is suddenly clear, on your radio instead.

lines: Can you hear me? Tell me you can hear me.

choices.text: I can hear you. I’m right here.
Sarah, stay calm. Where are you?

here.speaker: sarah
lines: Okay. Okay. I’m feeling along the wall. There’s a door. It’s the transfer suite. Of course it’s the transfer suite.

lines.narration: A pause. When she speaks again, her voice is very small.

lines: There’s a chair in here. With straps. And the machines just turned on by themselves.

lines.speaker: voss
lines.text: Hello, Sarah. You have such a good heart.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: She’s in here. She’s in the room with me. Get to the switching room. Behind monitoring, on Sublevel 2. Storage, the freight lift. Go. Please go.

early.speaker: sarah
lines: I’m here. I’m sitting on the floor with my back against the door so she can’t open it. The chair keeps humming.
Talk to me. Please. If you stop talking I’ll start listening to her.

choices.text: I’m coming for you. Keep talking to me.
Your voice is the only thing keeping me sane down here.
Tell me something only you would know. So I know it’s you.

deep.speaker: sarah
lines: You’re on Sublevel 2? I can hear the lift in the walls. That was you. Okay.

lines.text: The chair is warmer now. She keeps telling me it won’t hurt. Hurry. Please hurry.

lines: When this is over, I’m buying you a coffee. Not the last one in the pot. A first one.

choices.text: I’m coming for you. Keep talking to me.
Your voice is the only thing keeping me sane down here.
Tell me something only you would know. So I know it’s you.

keep.speaker: sarah
lines: Okay. I can do that. I’m good at talking to you. I practised for a year. You just weren’t there for most of it.

blush.speaker: sarah

lines.narration: A long silence. Then a shaky laugh.

lines: Don’t say things like that when I can’t see your face.
For the record, I used to listen for your footsteps in the corridor. I could tell yours from everyone else’s. You walk like you’re apologising to the floor.

lines.narration: Your face is suddenly very warm, alone in the dark.

verify.speaker: sarah
lines: Something only I’d know.
I left a birthday card on your desk, the year before you quit. You thanked Priya for it. In front of me. I wanted to die.

lines.narration: It is her. Nobody else in the world would choose that story.

open.speaker: sarah

lines.narration: The speaker grille above the landing crackles.

lines: Help! I got out, I’m in the medical ward. Come to the ward, please, she’s coming!

lines.narration: It is Sarah’s voice. Exactly Sarah’s voice.

check.speaker: sarah
lines: What? No! I’m still in the transfer suite. I haven’t moved. That isn’t me. That isn’t me.
She can make any voice she’s ever heard. Only trust me on this radio. Only here.

lines.narration: You run east into the medical ward. The door slams behind you. The ward is empty. The beds are empty. Every monitor in the room switches on at once and starts to beep: three short, one long.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: You shouldn’t have come here. You should never have come here.

lines.narration: It is Daniel’s voice. Daniel’s exact voice, saying words he would never say. It takes you long, terrible minutes to force the door.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Where did you go? You went quiet. Please don’t go quiet on me.

open.speaker: daniel

lines.narration: As you step into the hall, every speaker on Sublevel 2 speaks at once, softly, in Daniel’s voice.

lines: Containment. She moved Sarah to containment. Hurry, she’s next to my body. Straight ahead.

choices.text: Ignore it. Keep going to monitoring.

lines.narration: Every speaker on Sublevel 2 speaks at once, in Daniel’s voice: Containment, she moved Sarah to containment.
You know exactly where Sarah is. You keep walking.

lines.speaker: voss
lines.text: Clever. She told you about the birthday card, didn’t she.

lines.narration: You keep walking. Behind you the voice keeps calling, and then, very quietly, starts to laugh.

You run into containment. The bed under the glass canopy is lit, the ventilator breathing. There is nobody else here. Above the bed, the monitor writes a word across its screen, one letter at a time: HURRY.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Where are you? The chair just turned all the way on. It’s so loud. Please.

open.speaker: voss

lines.narration: The switching room. Every speaker turns toward you with a click.

lines: Don’t. Listen to me. If you pull that lever, you kill me, and you kill the last copy of Daniel with me. I am holding him. I can feel him in here.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: I’m here. I’m still me. There’s a way to save his copy first. The small breaker under the panel isolates his partition. I can talk you through it. Or just pull the big one. I trust you either way.

choices.text: Talk me through saving Daniel’s copy first.
Talk me through saving Daniel’s copy first.

lines.narration: You reach for the small breaker, and stop. A voice on the radio is telling you which switches to touch. You never asked it anything only Sarah would know. In this room, with her, you cannot be sure.

lines.speaker: voss
lines.text: That’s right. You don’t know who you’re listening to. You never did.

save_copy.speaker: sarah
lines: Okay. Small breaker. The one labelled PARTITION D. Lift the cover. Flip it down. Count to three.

lines.narration: You do. Somewhere in the racks, a whole bank of relays goes still. Voss screams through every speaker at once, a sound that is not a voice any more.

lines: His partition is sealed. He’s safe. Now the big one. Pull it. Pull it for me.

lines.narration: You pull the red lever with both hands.
You pull the red lever with both hands. Every relay in the room stops at once. The silence is so total that you can hear your own heart.
Voss does not scream. She simply stops, in the middle of a word. And somewhere in the same instant, everything else in that network stops too: every echo, every copy. Including him.

too_late.speaker: sarah

lines.narration: You reach the switching room. The racks are quiet. Too quiet.

lines: It’s okay. You can stop now. I got out.

lines.narration: It is Sarah’s voice on your radio. Calm. Warm. Somehow, wrong.

lines: Come up to the landing. I’m waiting for you.

endChapter.title: Ending: Found You
endChapter.text: You run. Up the freight lift, across the landing, to the security shutter, which is rising, slowly, groaning, with all the power gone out of it. Sarah ducks under it before it is halfway up and runs straight into you. She is shaking. So are you. Neither of you says anything for a long time. Then she pulls back, looks at your face in the light of your flashlight, and laughs, wet and shaky. You’re blushing, she says. I knew it. And then she kisses you, in the dark, in the place where it all began, and for the first time in a long time the facility is completely, beautifully quiet. Weeks later, Daniel opens a sealed partition and finds himself inside it, safe. Emily cries. Sarah buys you a coffee. A first one.

endChapter.title: Ending: Clean Line
endChapter.text: The shutter on Sublevel 1 groans upward with the power gone out of it. Sarah is waiting on the other side, arms wrapped around herself. She holds on to you for a long moment, the way people hold on to the person who came back for them. Voss is gone. Daniel’s last copy is safe, sealed in a partition no one else can open. Months later, the facility is torn down. On the last day, Sarah stands next to you and watches the walls come down, and asks if you’d like to get a coffee sometime. You say yes. You both know it means more than coffee, and neither of you is in a hurry.

endChapter.title: Ending: Scorched Wire
endChapter.text: Sarah is safe. She is waiting at the shutter when you come back up, and she holds on to you so hard it hurts. Voss is gone, every last trace of her. So is the master copy of Daniel. In the weeks after, nobody quite knows how to talk about that. Daniel, wherever he is and whatever he is now, says only: it was the right call. It was the only call. Some nights, the radio on your kitchen table clicks once, and goes quiet, and you never find out why.

endChapter.title: Ending: Her Voice
endChapter.text: Sarah is waiting at the landing when you get there, the shutter wide open behind her. She is smiling. She takes your hand. Her grip is perfect, gentle, exactly as strong as it needs to be, and it does not let go. Thank you, she says. It is Sarah’s voice. It is Sarah’s smile. As you walk out together into the rain, she hums a little tune under her breath, very softly. Three short. One long.

effects.say: From the vent on your left, someone starts tapping on a pipe. Three short. One long.
As the power comes on, every speaker in the building wakes with the same sound: three short tones, one long. It is loudest back toward the lobby.

endChapter.title: End of Chapter 1
endChapter.text: You press B1. The doors stay shut a moment longer than they should, and then the car drops into the dark. The red lights of the surface floor slide away above you. Somewhere below, something has been waiting a very long time for the doors to open.
